title: Medicals & Renewing Your Lorry Licence
whatItIs: You need a D4 medical to get a provisional lorry licence. You then renew every 5 years, with a new D4 medical from age 45, and every year from 65. Renewing is free.

keyFacts.text: You MUST tell DVLA about any health condition likely to affect your driving.

keyFacts: To apply for a provisional lorry licence, send form D2 and a D4 medical report filled in by a doctor.
Renew your lorry licence every 5 years, and every year once you reach 65. Renewing is free.
DVLA sends the renewal forms 56 days before your licence runs out.
Under 45: you renew with form D47PU. From 45: form D47P plus a D4 medical report from a doctor.
An optician or optometrist can fill in the eyesight part of the D4. They may charge for this.

visual.caption: Renewing a lorry licence: what DVLA sends you

notes: Licence runs out within 56 days of your 45th birthday? Follow the 45-and-over process.
Renewing a lorry licence and applying for a provisional bus licence? You may need a D4 too.

a.label: Renewing your lorry licence
points: Every 5 years (every year from 65), through DVLA
From 45, needs a D4 medical report

b.label: Keeping your Driver CPC
points: 35 hours of periodic training every 5 years
Recorded by DVSA; your deadline is on your Driver CPC card

onTheTest.question: You are 47 and your lorry licence is due for renewal. What must you send to DVLA with form D47P?
onTheTest.why: If you're 45 or over, DVLA sends you form D47P and a D4 medical examination report. A doctor must complete the D4.

onTheTest.question: How often must you renew your lorry licence once you reach 65?
onTheTest.why: You need to renew your bus or lorry licence every 5 years, and every year when you reach 65.

traps: Renewing is free, but the doctor, optician or optometrist may charge for the D4.
Your licence and your Driver CPC are separate: renewing one does not renew the other.
No forms through the post? Get a pack from a Post Office that offers DVLA services.
